registered_outcome_branch.registered_sentence_filled: Rerunning seed 42 in the seed-123/456 configuration gives S1-TTA 91.39 (seeds 123/456: 91.40, 91.10) and deepest-block separation 7.72 (7.85, 7.97). The 3.28 of the published seed-42 run therefore reflects its configuration (block_curr_lambda 0, depth_order_lambda 0), not seed variance.
required_qualifiers: the separation value is the last Stage-1 epoch (362); at the validation-selected epoch the new seed 42 gives 3.69 (epoch 200), close to the published seed 42's 3.22 (epoch 320) and below seeds 123/456 (5.65/6.41, epoch 260); see sep_convention_caveat
one re-run of one seed; it does not separate block_curr_lambda from depth_order_lambda
hardware: the new seed 42 ran on a Colab NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB; seeds 123/456 ran on a DGX Spark NVIDIA GB10; the published seed 42 also ran on a Colab NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
the new run was resumed twice (epoch-3 and epoch-274 checkpoints; RNG restored, DataLoader workers re-seeded)
registered_outcome_branch.scope_note: the registered sentence rests on one re-run seed: in the same seed and split, moving to the seed-123/456 loss weights moved the last-epoch deepest sep from 3.28 to 7.72 (both runs on Colab A100). So seed 42 with this split does not by itself produce the low last-epoch separation under the matched configuration. The evidence is one re-run. It does not separate block_curr_lambda from depth_order_lambda, and it does not exclude run-level nondeterminism (resumes; torch 2.10.0+cu128 vs 2.11.0+cu128; trainer code identity is verified only through config.json) as a smaller contributor

predictions.sep_convention_caveat: P2 is registered on the last Stage-1 epoch (362) and passes (7.72). The paper's tab:gamma0_multiseed note prints the separation at each run's validation-selected epoch (3.22/5.65/6.41 at epochs 320/260/260). On that convention the new seed 42 gives 3.69 at epoch 200: below seeds 123/456 and close to the published seed 42's 3.22, because its validation accuracy peaked 60 epochs earlier, while separation was still rising. At matched epochs the new run stays much closer to seeds 123/456 than to the published seed 42 (epoch 200: new 3.69, seeds 123/456 3.51/3.67, published seed 42 2.48), but it mostly sits slightly below them: at the 10 common evaluation epochs from 200 to 362 it lies 0.80 below to 0.10 above the seed-123/456 mean; it is below both seeds at 7, inside their range at 2 and above both at 1 of those epochs. The published seed 42 lies 1.11 to 4.86 below that mean (below both seeds at 10 of 10). Any sentence that uses the registered result must say that it refers to the last epoch, and it must also report the selected-epoch value.

disclosures: hardware mixing: the matched-config n = 3 combines the new seed 42, trained on a Colab NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (torch 2.11.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8, cuDNN 91900, Python 3.13.15, x86_64), with seeds 123/456, trained on a DGX Spark NVIDIA GB10 (torch 2.9.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 91300, Python 3.12.3, aarch64). Its SD therefore mixes seed and hardware/software variation. The published n = 3 mixes the same two platforms (published seed 42 on a Colab NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, torch 2.10.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8, cuDNN 91002, Python 3.12.12, x86_64), so the new-vs-published seed-42 comparison is on the same GPU model but not the same software stack.

resumes: the new seed-42 run was trained in 4 Colab segments; 2 resumes (from the epoch-3 checkpoint into segment 3 and from the epoch-274 checkpoint into segment 4), both with rng_restored = true in events.jsonl. The persistent DataLoader workers are re-seeded on resume, so the run is reproducible from its checkpoints but not bitwise equal to an uninterrupted run.

segment 2's console log reports Stage-1 checkpoint saves for epochs 1-4, but segment 3 loaded the epoch-3 checkpoint, so the last logged save did not persist on Drive (most likely not yet synced when the CLI VM was lost; inference, not recorded in the files); epoch 4 was therefore trained twice

selected checkpoint: the validation-selected Stage-1 epoch is 200 (val 0.9128) in ff_cifar10_cifar10_gamma0_seed42_matched_L4_D256_bs512_seed42_20260926_105045; S1/S1-TTA therefore come from a backbone trained in segments 2-3 only; the Stage-2 head (S2/S2-TTA) and the epoch-362 sep (P2) come from segment 4, after the second resume

console log: the Drive trainer log has no trainer output for segment 3 (START header only) and no header for segment 1; segment 3 is documented by its run-directory jsonl files; its CUDA-RNG restore is not separately recorded (events.jsonl records rng_restored = true; segment 4's console line confirms python, numpy, torch CPU and torch CUDA)

checkpoint files are on Google Drive only and were not inspected; the selected epoch is identified from the logs (first val eval attaining best_s1, strict '>' update), as in results/e1_tier1_sep_acc.json

software differs from the plan's note: the F2 segments ran torch 2.11.0+cu128 with Python 3.13.15 and cuDNN 91900 (PREDICTIONS.md listed the published seed 42's torch 2.10.0+cu128 and CR/.venv's 2.14.0+cu130 as known differences)
